purpose: Visual reference descriptions for category and model recognition from a query image, including unfamiliar viewing angles.

provenance.method: Manual visual inspection of embedded original-resolution images. No manufacturer specifications or multi-view photographs were supplied.
provenance.model_name_policy: Names and numeric IDs are copied exactly from the source; names do not independently prove brand, material or mechanical properties.
provenance.scope: All 36 thumbnail entries in the Type 0 lexicon: 32 physical model photographs and four category fallback icons. Etat and Commentaires are not image/model categories.
provenance.angle_limit: Viewpoint guidance is a geometric interpretation of the visible reference, not confirmation of unseen surfaces. Descriptions alone cannot guarantee recognition from every angle.

feature_priority: Overall topology and arrangement of parts
Head, lid, arm, infill or loop shape
Surface pattern and broad material appearance
Colour and condition only as secondary evidence
nuisance_factors: Ignore photo background, pavement, vehicles, vegetation, shadows and nearby objects.
Allow changes in viewpoint, scale, lighting, paint, dirt, wear, bags and temporary stickers.
Treat an occluded feature as unknown, not absent.
Do not use image pixel dimensions as physical object dimensions.
Mirror left/right expectations when observing the opposite side; preserve top/bottom relationships.
recognition_policy.generic_label_policy: banc_banc, barriere_barriere, potelet_borne and potelet_potelet are specific predefined entries, not category fallbacks.

decisions.matched: Sufficient visible diagnostic evidence for one predefined model, with no strong visible contradiction.
decisions.category_fallback: Known category, sufficiently visible design, and positive structural evidence that none of its predefined models fits.
decisions.ambiguous: Two or more predefined models remain plausible and visible features do not separate them.
decisions.insufficient_evidence: An object is visible but blur, crop, occlusion or viewpoint prevents reliable category or model recognition.
decisions.out_of_scope: The object is sufficiently visible but does not belong to a catalogue category.

recognition_policy.uncertainty_rule: Leave model name and model ID null for ambiguous, insufficient_evidence and out_of_scope. A lack of certainty is not positive evidence of an unlisted model.
recognition_policy.required_comparison: For a specific match, seek two independent structural cues when visible. These cues support a decision but are not a calibrated statistical threshold. Resolve close competitors explicitly or abstain.

known_ambiguities.reason: Mechanical shape-memory behaviour is not inferable from these still references; ordinary query views can be visually indistinguishable.
Require a resolved central ornament to distinguish raised rosette from plain disc.
Plain cylinders differ subtly at the crown and finish; low-resolution or head-cropped images can be ambiguous.

categories.category_description: An elongated human seating object, with a horizontal seat supported above ground, with or without backrest or armrests. Include sculptural seating. Use the relationship between seat, back, arms and supports rather than surrounding people or location.

images.semantic_description: The query object belongs to bench category, but its adequately visible design falls outside every predefined model in this category.
images.selection_rule: Use only when category membership is clear and visible structural evidence supports an unlisted design after comparing all predefined models. Do not use merely because resolution, viewpoint, cropping or occlusion prevents a model decision.
images.viewpoint_guidance: Recognize the physical category from the query image. Never look for a question-mark symbol on the object.
limitations: This icon contains no physical model geometry.
Not a synonym for insufficient evidence, and not a category for objects outside the four catalogue categories.

images.name: banc_banc
images.visual_description: A conventional elongated public bench with warm brown, wood-like horizontal slats and a dark grey metal frame. The backrest has one noticeably broad upper plank above three narrower horizontal strips, separated by open gaps. Upright metal supports divide the backrest at its ends and near the middle. The seat is made of several parallel longitudinal boards, with a rounded front edge, above a straight metal apron. The frame has straight, angular legs and a central support visible below the seat. The ends of the seat and back are connected by angular side framing; there are no prominent curved armrest loops. The dominant visual contrast is broad wooden planks against rectangular metal members.
diagnostic_features: Broad top back plank plus three slimmer back strips
Brown longitudinal seat boards with rounded front edge
Straight angular grey frame and central back support
No conspicuous circular side-arm ornament
images.viewpoint_guidance: From the rear, seek the same horizontal board pattern and vertical metal supports. From an end, use the angular leg/seat/back structure and board cross-sections; plank counts may be hidden by perspective. A front view can conceal the seat depth and rear legs.

confusable_with.name: banc_bercy
confusable_with.distinction: Bercy has many fine metal rods and semicircular ornamental arm structures rather than broad wood-like planks.

confusable_with.name: banc_sedis_torsion
confusable_with.distinction: Sedis torsion has a continuous twisting plank ribbon and pedestal supports rather than an ordinary upright back and angular frame.

limitations: Wood species, exact dimensions and hidden fasteners cannot be established.
Despite the generic source name, this is a specific visual reference, not the fallback for every bench.

images.name: banc_bercy
images.visual_description: A dark metal bench with a rectangular, slightly reclined back and a slatted seat. Both surfaces are composed of numerous thin, closely spaced parallel metal rods or narrow strips, producing a fine grille texture rather than a few broad boards. At each end a large tubular semicircular arch forms a raised armrest and continues into the side support. Inside that arch is a smaller concentric curved element and a dark semicircular central ornament near seat level. Rounded legs end on small ground-fixing plates. A substantial perimeter frame encloses the fine backrest grille. The combination of dense narrow metal slats and nested semicircular end details is especially distinctive.
diagnostic_features: Dense fine metal grille on seat and back
Large semicircular tubular armrests at both ends
Smaller concentric arch and semicircular insert within each end
Rectangular perimeter around backrest
images.viewpoint_guidance: An end-on view should emphasize the nested arch motif even when the seat rods merge visually. A rear view still exposes the fine back grille and curved end frames. At distance the rods can alias into a solid dark surface, so avoid treating invisible gaps as absent.

confusable_with.name: banc_banc
confusable_with.distinction: Uses a few broad wooden boards and angular side framing.

confusable_with.name: banc_sedis_torsion
confusable_with.distinction: Uses broad flowing planks and lacks the nested semicircular arms.

limitations: Do not require black paint; repainting and lighting may change apparent colour.
Rod count is not a reliable recognition criterion.

images.name: banc_sedis_torsion
images.visual_description: A sculptural, elongated bench made of several broad golden-brown wood-like strips that form a flowing, folded ribbon. In the main visible section the strips create a seat and a backrest with rounded transitions. Toward the farther end the arrangement twists and rises into a narrow, almost horizontal perch, changing the orientation of the seating surface along the bench. The near end exposes the thick plank profiles, including a small projecting return at the top of the back. Several dark tapered pedestal legs with ground plates support the ribbon from below. There are no conventional armrest hoops or simple rectangular end frames. The continuous change of surface orientation is more diagnostic than the yellow-brown finish.
diagnostic_features: Broad continuous strips following a twisting or folding seat/back profile
Transition from backed seating to a raised narrow perch
Dark tapered pedestal supports
Rounded plank edges and no conventional armrests
images.viewpoint_guidance: From an end, examine the folded cross-section of the seat and back. From the rear or opposite end, look for the transition along the length rather than expecting the same left-to-right silhouette. A tight crop of a straight section may conceal the distinctive twist.

confusable_with.name: banc_banc
confusable_with.distinction: Has an ordinary separate straight backrest, a few horizontal boards and an angular metal frame.

limitations: Only one perspective is documented; the entire opposite side is not directly observed.
If the twist and supports are hidden, do not infer this model from wood colour alone.

categories.category_description: A low freestanding or fixed railing/panel intended to separate pedestrian and vehicle spaces, usually with two lateral supports and a spanning rail, sometimes with infill. Do not classify a gate or fence panel from context alone; inspect its construction. The catalogue keeps bicycle stands in potelet.

images.name: barriere_2000_vague_vers_le_bat_et_chapeau_classique
images.visual_description: A pedestrian barrier panel with two cylindrical outer posts, a round top rail and a round low rail. Within the rectangular opening, a broad flat decorative element forms two long bowed edges separated by a tapered open slot. In this reference the edges come together near the upper rail and spread apart toward the lower rail, making a downward-opening, elongated wave or fork. Both posts project above the top rail and terminate in contrasting bright rounded mushroom-like caps with a narrow collar or neck beneath. The main frame is grey. The direction in which the inner opening widens and the raised traditional cap profile distinguish this entry from the other wave barrier.
diagnostic_features: Round posts and two horizontal round rails
Curved double-edged infill: narrow/joined at top, wider at bottom
Bright raised mushroom-like caps and neck/collar detail
No central X intersection
images.viewpoint_guidance: Viewed from the other side, the curve may reverse horizontally, but its top-narrow/bottom-wide relationship remains. At oblique angles the two infill edges may overlap; inspect caps and the connection to both rails. Do not use left-versus-right curvature as the discriminator.

confusable_with.name: barriere_2000_vague_vers_le_haut_et_chapeau_contemporain
confusable_with.distinction: The other wave narrows/joins at the bottom, opens toward the top, and has low-profile cylindrical caps.

limitations: The source label contains "bat"; preserve it exactly for output rather than correcting to "bas".
Cap shape or wave direction must be visible to separate the two models confidently.

images.name: barriere_2000_vague_vers_le_haut_et_chapeau_contemporain
images.visual_description: A grey barrier with two round vertical posts and round horizontal top and bottom rails. The opening contains two broad curving metal edges that meet in a narrow bridge at the lower rail and diverge toward the upper rail. Together they form a tall, open-ended, upward-widening curved fork or wave. The slot ends in a rounded turn near the bottom. The outer posts extend a short distance above the top rail and have restrained, low cylindrical caps of approximately the post diameter, with a shallow seam below the top. Unlike the traditional-cap version, there is no prominently projecting bright mushroom finial.
diagnostic_features: Curved infill joined/narrow at bottom and open/wide at top
Rounded bottom of elongated inner slot
Round posts and round top/bottom rails
Low cylindrical post caps with subtle seams
images.viewpoint_guidance: Use gravity-relative top and bottom when comparing views; viewing the rear reverses left and right but not the narrow lower junction. In a side view, the wave can collapse into a single strip. A cropped top should reduce confidence in the cap comparison.

confusable_with.name: barriere_2000_vague_vers_le_bat_et_chapeau_classique
confusable_with.distinction: Has the wave joined near the top and wider at the bottom, plus raised mushroom-like caps.

limitations: The reference is slightly blurred; small seams are secondary evidence.
Paint colour is shared with many unrelated barriers.

images.name: barriere_arceau
images.visual_description: A red-brown painted rectangular pedestrian barrier, taller-looking than wide in the supplied view. Two upright side members support a straight top rail and a low bottom rail. Two thin diagonal members form a full X between opposite corners. Their crossing is covered by a conspicuous raised, irregular, flower- or rosette-like ornamental boss. The straight top rail projects slightly beyond the side uprights. The decorative centre has visible relief, unlike a simple flat circular joining plate. Although the label contains "arceau", the pictured object is a rectangular X-braced barrier, not a plain inverted-U bicycle hoop.
diagnostic_features: Rectangular frame containing a full diagonal X
Raised ornate rosette-like central boss
Top rail projects beyond uprights
Thin diagonal members rather than wave infill
images.viewpoint_guidance: In a frontal view, prioritize the central ornament and X. From the rear the ornamental face may be less distinct or invisible; the source does not show its rear treatment. Oblique perspective changes apparent panel width, so aspect ratio is only supporting evidence.

confusable_with.name: barriere_odeon
confusable_with.distinction: Also an X barrier but shows a plain flat circular centre rather than a raised rosette.

confusable_with.name: barriere_barriere
confusable_with.distinction: Uses a branching Y-like pair of uprights and collar, not an X.

limitations: Do not assign from the name "arceau" alone.
If the centre is too small to resolve, the X-barrier model should remain ambiguous.

images.name: barriere_barriere
images.visual_description: A dark blue-grey rectangular barrier with a straight top rail, side uprights and a low bottom rail. Its infill is not a full X: two slender bars descend diagonally from the upper corners, curve inward near the centre, and then continue as two closely spaced parallel vertical stems to the bottom rail. A thick horizontal collar binds the paired bars around the point where they become vertical. This produces a symmetrical branching Y or funnel outline with a doubled central stem. The large open regions on either side of the stem extend down to the lower corners.
diagnostic_features: Two upper diagonal branches converge into paired vertical lower stems
Prominent small collar around centre junction
No diagonals from the centre to lower corners
Straight rectangular outer frame
images.viewpoint_guidance: From the rear, the doubled-stem topology should remain the same. In an oblique view the two stems can visually overlap; look for the curved transition from upper branches to a lower upright and for the collar. Colour and exact width are weak clues.

confusable_with.name: barriere_arceau
confusable_with.distinction: Full X with a raised rosette at the crossing.

confusable_with.name: barriere_odeon
confusable_with.distinction: Full X with a flat central disc.

limitations: The generic label is a specific model entry, not an unknown-barrier category.

images.name: barriere_delinea
images.visual_description: A minimalist two-post guardrail with a single substantial round horizontal tube at the top. The tube has a bright metallic finish and closed circular ends; it extends beyond both supporting uprights. Each upright is a narrow dark rust-brown rectangular member rather than a round post, with visible small fasteners near its upper attachment. Short connectors lift the rail slightly above the uprights. The uprights terminate on flat rectangular ground plates with corner fixings. There is no lower rail, central lattice, cross brace or decorative infill: the area below the top tube is entirely open.
diagnostic_features: One overhanging bright cylindrical top rail
Two dark narrow rectangular uprights
Small offset connectors between posts and rail
Open lower area, with no bottom rail or infill
images.viewpoint_guidance: From an end, the round tube cross-section and rectangular post contrast are useful. From either long side, the open bay and two-material construction remain diagnostic. Ground plates may disappear in vegetation or a tight crop and are not required.

confusable_with.name: barriere_barriere
confusable_with.distinction: Has a complete rectangular frame, bottom rail and branching infill.

limitations: Bright metal and rust-coloured surfaces suggest material classes but do not certify their alloys.
A crop containing only the top tube is insufficient.

images.name: barriere_odeon
images.visual_description: A dark green rectangular pedestrian barrier with a broad-looking horizontal top member, straight side posts and a slim bottom member. Two straight diagonal strips form a full X, meeting at a small plain round disc in the middle. The disc appears flat and unornamented. The supplied panel looks wider than tall, with the top rail extending slightly beyond the side members. The overall treatment is simple and geometric: straight members, four triangular openings around the centre, and no raised floral ornament, curved wave, or doubled lower stem.
diagnostic_features: Full straight X inside rectangular frame
Small plain circular central plate
No sculpted rosette at crossing
Straight bottom and top rails
images.viewpoint_guidance: The X and centre-disc arrangement is useful from both broad sides, although the rear attachment is not documented. From a shallow angle the centre disc may appear elliptical and the X foreshortened. Do not require the reference width-to-height ratio under perspective.

confusable_with.name: barriere_arceau
confusable_with.distinction: Its centre is a raised ornate rosette rather than a plain flat disc.

confusable_with.name: barriere_barriere
confusable_with.distinction: Has upper branches and paired vertical stems rather than a full X.

limitations: Arceau versus Odeon may be unresolved when the central fitting is occluded or low resolution.

images.name: corbeille_conga
images.visual_description: A freestanding cylindrical litter bin in a dark rust-brown finish. A broad flat circular top plate forms an annulus around a central round disposal opening. Most of the curved outer body is pierced with large irregular interlocking shapes: arcs, leaf-like slivers, rounded fragments and angular pieces, producing an open abstract mosaic rather than uniform rows of holes. Solid bands remain near the top and bottom. The pierced shell allows the darker interior or liner to show through. There is no elevated rain canopy and no separate tall side support frame.
diagnostic_features: Cylindrical shell with large irregular abstract cutouts
Flat ring-shaped top with central opening
Solid upper/lower bands around patterned body
No regular horizontal slit or diamond-stud pattern
images.viewpoint_guidance: Around the cylinder the exact cutout arrangement may differ, but the irregular large-scale openwork should remain useful. From above, the ring lid is shared with other bins and must be combined with side-wall evidence. Rust tone can vary with age and lighting.

confusable_with.name: corbeille_corten_spencer_ronde
confusable_with.distinction: Has a smooth solid cylindrical shell with no abstract perforations.

confusable_with.name: corbeille_contemporaine
confusable_with.distinction: Has evenly spaced horizontal slits rather than irregular cutouts.

limitations: The reference suggests weathered metal; the exact alloy is not established by appearance.
Contents visible through holes are not model features.

images.name: corbeille_contemporaine
images.visual_description: A cylindrical grey metal litter bin with a broad overhanging flat ring lid and a circular central opening. The side wall is dominated by many regularly spaced narrow horizontal slots running around the cylinder. These slots alternate with solid thin bands and reveal an inner liner. Narrow vertical strips interrupt the slot pattern near the sides. A wide solid lower band forms the base area, while a shorter solid collar sits beneath the lid. A small hinge or fastening tab is visible near the upper rim. The dense repeated horizontal rhythm is the main distinguishing feature.
diagnostic_features: Regular horizontal slots across most of cylindrical body
Wide solid lower band
Overhanging annular lid with central opening
Inner liner visible through narrow slits
images.viewpoint_guidance: From any side, seek repeated horizontal bands; foreshortening may compress them but should not turn them into a random pattern. From above, rely less on the shared ring lid and seek a visible portion of the slotted side. Vertical seams can vary in visibility.

confusable_with.name: corbeille_conga
confusable_with.distinction: Large irregular abstract perforations, not uniform horizontal slots.

confusable_with.name: corbeille_ronde_pointes_de_diamant
confusable_with.distinction: Small raised diamond-like points and a central pedestal rather than horizontal slots.

limitations: The exact slot count and grey finish are not hard requirements.

images.name: corbeille_corten_spencer_ronde
images.visual_description: A tall simple cylindrical litter bin with a mostly smooth, uninterrupted rust-brown sheet-metal body. A broad flat circular ring at the top surrounds the round disposal opening and overhangs the side wall slightly. Small fittings or brackets are visible immediately under the rim, and a narrow vertical body seam runs down one side. The shell is solid rather than perforated or slatted. A small bright rim is visible at ground level in the reference. The visual signature is the plain weathered cylinder plus open-centred flat top, with no canopy, ornate pattern, or large separate support legs.
diagnostic_features: Smooth solid cylindrical body
Rust-brown mottled finish in reference
Flat annular lid with central opening
Vertical seam and small fittings under rim
images.viewpoint_guidance: A side view may hide the top opening but should still show the plain cylinder and overhanging rim. A rear view may move or hide the seam. Use the absence of openwork only when a substantial portion of the side wall is visible.

confusable_with.name: corbeille_conga
confusable_with.distinction: Has extensive irregular decorative cutouts.

confusable_with.name: corbeille_contemporaine
confusable_with.distinction: Has many horizontal slots and a different side-wall texture.

limitations: The label specifies corten; the photograph alone only supports a rust-like surface.
A plain cylindrical bin of another design must not be matched solely on brown colour.

images.name: corbeille_ecolor
images.visual_description: An open-frame bag-holding litter bin attached to a single round side post. The reference is bright blue. A broad circular upper lid or rim has a large central opening and is hinged or clamped near the post. Below it, a transparent refuse sack is exposed inside a very open cage of widely spaced horizontal circular hoops, with slender connecting rods. There is no continuous sheet-metal basket wall. Clamps wrap around the side post near the top and lower section. The flexible bag, open hoop cage and single side-mounted support distinguish it from the solid cylindrical bins.
diagnostic_features: Visible flexible bag inside widely spaced circular hoops
One round support post along the side
Top ring/lid attached near post with clamp/hinge
No continuous rigid side-wall shell
images.viewpoint_guidance: From the side opposite the post, the post may be hidden behind the bag; use the sparse hoop cage and exposed sack. From above, inspect the hinge-to-post connection. The bag may be absent or opaque, so require the supporting cage rather than transparency itself.

confusable_with.name: corbeille_contemporaine
confusable_with.distinction: Has dense slots cut into a rigid cylindrical shell, not a sparse hoop cage around a bag.

limitations: Blue paint and current bag contents are incidental.
Do not confuse a missing bag with a different model if the frame matches.

images.name: corbeille_pointes_de_diamant
images.visual_description: A suspended cylindrical or rounded basket mounted between two tall rectangular side uprights. The basket surface is covered by a dense regular grid of tiny raised diamond- or pyramid-like points. It stops well above ground, leaving open space underneath. A separate flat oval-looking cover, circular or rounded in plan, spans the tops of the two uprights above the basket mouth, creating a wide horizontal gap for depositing litter beneath the canopy. The opening is therefore under a raised roof rather than a central hole in a lid flush with the basket. The reference is light grey, and the upright supports extend down to the ground on both sides.
diagnostic_features: Two tall rectangular side supports
Raised flat canopy with open gap above basket rim
Dense grid of small raised points on basket
Basket suspended clear of ground
images.viewpoint_guidance: A side-on view may overlap the two supports; look for the gap under the elevated cover and for the suspended basket. From a high angle, avoid mistaking the solid canopy for a ring lid. The stud pattern alone cannot separate the two diamond-point models.

confusable_with.name: corbeille_ronde_pointes_de_diamant
confusable_with.distinction: Has a flush annular top opening and one central cylindrical pedestal instead of a raised canopy and two long side legs.

limitations: Exact canopy plan shape is uncertain from this perspective.
If the lid and support arrangement are hidden, the diamond-point subtype may remain ambiguous.

images.name: corbeille_ronde_pointes_de_diamant
images.visual_description: A round litter basket whose cylindrical body is covered in orderly rows and columns of small raised diamond- or pyramid-like points. The flat circular lid sits directly on the basket and has a central round disposal hole. The basket is supported on one substantial central cylindrical pedestal, visibly narrower than the basket, which reaches the ground. A small rectangular external fitting or latch is visible high on one side. Unlike the other diamond-point bin, this model has no separate elevated roof and no pair of full-height outer support legs.
diagnostic_features: Studded cylindrical basket
Flush flat ring lid with central disposal hole
Single narrower cylindrical pedestal beneath basket
No elevated rain canopy
images.viewpoint_guidance: From a low or side view, the centred narrower pedestal is particularly helpful. From above the opening distinguishes it from the solid raised canopy of the other studded bin. The latch may move out of view around the cylinder and is secondary.

confusable_with.name: corbeille_pointes_de_diamant
confusable_with.distinction: Suspended between two side legs under a separate raised canopy.

confusable_with.name: corbeille_contemporaine
confusable_with.distinction: Horizontal side-wall slots rather than a studded grid.

limitations: Do not treat grey colour or point count as decisive.
Supports can be occluded by nearby objects or vegetation.

categories.category_description: A short ground-fixed post used for separation, or one of the bicycle support stands deliberately grouped under this category by the source. For a post compare head, neck, shaft and foot; for a bicycle stand compare loop topology, central or paired supports, and cladding.

images.name: potelet_a_chapeau
images.visual_description: A slender round bollard with a smooth straight cylindrical shaft and an ornate projecting top. The upper ornament resembles a tiered hat: a broad rounded torus-like brim projects noticeably beyond the shaft and supports progressively smaller stepped or tapered rings above it. The visible finish is dark teal-green. The shaft itself has no prominent intermediate grooves, side hoops, or decorative rings. The photograph crops the very uppermost part of the ornament, so the complete finial profile is not documented. The wide tiered brim is a stronger identifier than the paint colour.
diagnostic_features: Smooth cylindrical shaft
Wide projecting rounded brim at top
Several smaller stepped tiers above brim
No side bicycle loop
images.viewpoint_guidance: The circular hat profile should be similar around the post. A high viewpoint can hide the neck below the brim; a low viewpoint can hide the upper tiers. If the head is outside the frame, the plain shaft is not enough for recognition.

confusable_with.name: potelet_serie_2000_les_classiques
confusable_with.distinction: Has a much smaller bright mushroom cap and narrow neck rather than a broad tiered hat.

confusable_with.name: potelet_potelet
confusable_with.distinction: Has a large ball finial, pronounced shoulder and decorated base.

limitations: Top of reference is cropped; do not invent the unseen peak.

images.name: potelet_a_gorge
images.visual_description: A plain cylindrical post with a short cylindrical head separated from the main shaft by a distinctly recessed circumferential neck or groove. Below that neck is a small rounded collar where the shaft resumes its normal diameter. The head has a flat or only gently rounded top. In the reference the body is dark brown-grey and a red-and-white diagonally striped adhesive band wraps around the upper shaft, below the groove. The strip is an accessory, not proof of model identity. There is no large ball, wide hat brim, or bicycle hoop.
diagnostic_features: Cylindrical head above a recessed circumferential neck
Smooth round straight shaft
Small shoulder/collar below groove
No side attachment visible
images.viewpoint_guidance: A circumferential groove should be detectable from multiple sides if resolution and lighting allow. The tape may be absent, damaged or on a different side. From above or with the head cropped, this can be indistinguishable from other plain posts.

confusable_with.name: potelet_a_gorge_a_memoire_de_forme
confusable_with.distinction: Very similar visible head and groove; flexibility/shape memory cannot be determined from an ordinary still image.

confusable_with.name: potelet_city
confusable_with.distinction: Shows a more conspicuous raised rounded bead beneath its cap.

limitations: Cannot reliably separate from the shape-memory entry on geometry alone in these references.
Never use the red-white tape as a mandatory or exclusive cue.

images.name: potelet_a_gorge_a_memoire_de_forme
images.visual_description: A smooth dark brown cylindrical bollard with a short rounded cylindrical top section and a narrow recessed ring immediately below it. The shaft continues straight to the ground at essentially uniform diameter. The visible groove makes the head appear slightly detached from the body in profile. There are no visible side loops, flared base or large projecting finial. The source name says "à mémoire de forme", but the photograph shows an upright static object and does not demonstrate bending, recovery, elasticity, or its internal construction. Its visual appearance is close to the other à-gorge post.
diagnostic_features: Smooth cylindrical shaft
Short cylindrical cap above narrow recessed ring
Simple ground insertion with no visible broad foot
No unique visual demonstration of shape-memory property
images.viewpoint_guidance: Use the head-and-groove silhouette as family-level evidence around the post. A change of view is unlikely to reveal its mechanical behaviour. Keep both à-gorge variants as candidates when no external identifying evidence is available.

confusable_with.name: potelet_a_gorge
confusable_with.distinction: No dependable geometry-only separation established; tape on that reference is incidental.

confusable_with.name: potelet_city
confusable_with.distinction: City has a more rounded projecting ring under the cap, but blur can hide this distinction.

limitations: Shape-memory functionality is source-label information, not an observed visual property.
Do not infer flexible material from a smooth dark surface.

images.name: potelet_a_gorge_plus_anneaux
images.visual_description: A weathered greenish bollard with a cylindrical shaft, short cylindrical head and narrowed neck below the head. A small metal loop or eye hangs or projects from the upper neck area on the visible side. The lower shaft flares outward into a broad bell- or skirt-like foot with a roughly square ground footprint. The reference surface is mottled with green and yellow weathering. The useful combination is the grooved head, side attachment eye and wide flared foot; neither the surface patina nor the presence of an attached chain is necessary.
diagnostic_features: Grooved neck under cylindrical head
Visible small side eye/loop near neck
Pronounced outward-flaring foot
Broad roughly square base footprint
images.viewpoint_guidance: The attachment eye may be hidden on the far side, while the flared base remains visible from most directions. If the base is buried or cropped, do not confuse the head alone with the ordinary à-gorge models. No unseen additional rings should be assumed.

confusable_with.name: potelet_a_gorge
confusable_with.distinction: Reference has a simple narrow shaft-to-ground profile without the broad flared base or visible eye.

confusable_with.name: potelet_borne
confusable_with.distinction: Much squat­ter, with two thick integral ring mouldings and a round plinth rather than a small attachment eye.

limitations: Only one small attachment loop is clearly visible; the plural source name does not establish the number on unseen sides.

images.name: potelet_borne
images.visual_description: A short, very stout decorative bollard with a broad cylindrical upper body and a flat round top. Two thick rounded ring mouldings encircle the upper portion, one below the top head and a second below that. The main body then narrows slightly before spreading into a broad bell-shaped foot on a substantial circular plinth. The reference is green and has a rough painted surface. It reads as a low, heavy, rotationally symmetric stump rather than a slender post. The double raised torus bands and the circular flared base are more distinctive than its colour.
diagnostic_features: Squat broad body
Two thick raised encircling rings near top
Bell-shaped flare into a wide circular plinth
Flat circular top, no ball
images.viewpoint_guidance: The ring-and-flare silhouette should remain similar around the object. A top-down image compresses its apparent height, so compare the concentric top and base features. Without a ground reference, do not claim an absolute height.

confusable_with.name: potelet_a_gorge_plus_anneaux
confusable_with.distinction: Slender post with a small side eye and more square-looking foot, not two large raised torus mouldings.

confusable_with.name: potelet_potelet
confusable_with.distinction: Has a large spherical finial and a more ornate polygonal lower base.

limitations: The generic word borne is a source model label, not the fallback for any stout bollard.

images.name: potelet_borne_a_velo
images.visual_description: A bicycle stand formed by a thick round tube bent into a tall inverted U with two separate legs anchored to small round ground plates. A straight horizontal crossbar spans between the legs below the rounded arch. Beneath that bar, an asymmetrical flat panel fills part of one side and tapers down toward a leg. The panel contains a small cluster of decorative cutouts. Much of the lower opening remains empty. The reference is grey. The combined U-hoop, crossbar and one-sided triangular infill distinguishes it from the centrally supported loop stands.
diagnostic_features: Rounded inverted-U outer tube with two ground legs
Straight crossbar below arch
Asymmetric tapered panel with small cutouts
Separate round fixing plates under legs
images.viewpoint_guidance: From the rear the asymmetric panel switches apparent sides. From edge-on, the panel and U can collapse visually; look for two ground contacts and the rounded tube. Do not require the exact decorative cutout to be resolved at distance.

confusable_with.name: potelet_borne_a_velo_2
confusable_with.distinction: Has one central upright, a straight upper bar and a broad curved lower arc.

confusable_with.name: potelet_borne_a_velo_ventoux
confusable_with.distinction: One wood-faced central support with rounded triangular tubular wings.

limitations: Bicycle stands are intentionally grouped under potelet in this catalogue.
The tiny cutout motif is not resolved enough to identify reliably.

images.name: potelet_borne_a_velo_2
images.visual_description: A bicycle support with one central upright combining grey metal and a long pale wood-like rectangular facing. A straight horizontal round bar crosses the top and extends equally to both sides. Its ends turn downward into a broad curved lower arc, creating a shallow bowl or semicircular outline hanging below the straight top. The central upright divides the open shape into two halves and continues downward to a single ground insertion. The curved side elements look relatively flat and slender compared with the top tube. There are no two separate outer legs reaching the ground.
diagnostic_features: Single central wood-faced vertical support
Straight top bar spanning both sides
Broad semicircular/bowl-shaped lower arc
One central ground contact
images.viewpoint_guidance: From the other face the wood facing may be less visible; use the central support and straight-top/curved-bottom loop. From an end, the loop becomes narrow and may be unrecognizable. Perspective can make the semicircle appear asymmetric.

confusable_with.name: potelet_borne_a_velo_ventoux
confusable_with.distinction: Uses a more rounded triangular outline with diagonal lower sides and thick dark tubing.

confusable_with.name: potelet_borne_velo_corten_cafe
confusable_with.distinction: Uses near-circular open side arcs and a split metal central column without a broad wood facing.

limitations: Wood appearance is observed; wood species is unknown.
Opposite-face cladding is not documented.

images.name: potelet_borne_a_velo_ventoux
images.visual_description: A centrally supported bicycle stand with a tall orange-brown wood-like rectangular face on its middle post. A continuous thick dark green tube spreads out to both sides near the top, rounds the outer corners, and slopes diagonally inward toward a lower central connection. Its overall outline resembles a wide rounded triangle or butterfly-like pair of wings with a nearly horizontal top. The broad central wooden facing covers the middle of the loop and extends below it. The lower sides are comparatively diagonal rather than forming a continuous deep semicircle. There is one central ground support.
diagnostic_features: Broad wood-faced central post
Thick tubular loop with rounded outer corners
Wide triangular wings with diagonal lower sides
Single central support to ground
images.viewpoint_guidance: The opposite broad side should still show the rounded triangular tube geometry even if the wood panel is hidden. At oblique angles compare tubing thickness and the diagonal lower outline rather than apparent total width. A side-on view may be insufficient.

confusable_with.name: potelet_borne_a_velo_2
confusable_with.distinction: Has a pale central panel, straight top and a more smoothly semicircular lower arc with flatter side members.

confusable_with.name: potelet_borne_velo_corten_cafe
confusable_with.distinction: Has a circular split-ring silhouette and no broad wood-faced centre.

limitations: Dark green and orange-brown colours are supporting cues only.
The back of the central post is not visible in the reference.

images.name: potelet_borne_velo_corten_cafe
images.visual_description: A rust-brown bicycle stand with an almost circular loop split into left and right curved flat-metal arcs. The arcs join a tall narrow central frame made of two parallel vertical members with a gap between them. Short horizontal bridges connect these members, including one high in the frame and another above a short solid lower section. At the top there is an open interruption between the two sides rather than a complete uninterrupted ring. The arcs attach lower down to the central frame, while the central post continues to a rectangular ground plate with visible corner fixings. No broad wooden face covers the central opening.
diagnostic_features: Near-circular split loop made of flat metal arcs
Twin narrow vertical central members with open gap
Short cross-bridges and solid lower central section
Rust-like finish and rectangular fixing plate
images.viewpoint_guidance: From either broad side, prioritize the circular arcs and split open central column. Edge-on, the flat strips can become almost invisible. Distinguish the target stand from adjacent repeated stands; overlapping neighbouring arcs should not be counted as extra parts.

confusable_with.name: potelet_borne_a_velo_2
confusable_with.distinction: Straight top bar and bowl-shaped lower arc around a broad wood-faced upright.

confusable_with.name: potelet_moka_corten
confusable_with.distinction: Similar open upright aesthetic but has no large circular side arcs.

limitations: The reference includes part of a second stand; only describe the foreground unit.
Rust finish is not sufficient to identify corten alloy.

images.name: potelet_borne_vision_corten
images.visual_description: A solid rectangular-section upright with a broad flat front and weathered rust-brown surfaces. A long narrow white rectangular inset is centred on the visible broad face, extending over much of the middle portion but leaving substantial metal margins above, below and on both sides. The top is closed and approximately flat. The post stands on a rectangular metal base plate with visible fixings. It has neither a round shaft nor an open frame. The pale inset appears opaque and could be a diffuser or panel, but active illumination is not shown in the photograph.
diagnostic_features: Solid rectangular column
Long centred white inset on broad front face
Closed top and broad rust-coloured margins
Rectangular bolted base plate
images.viewpoint_guidance: From the rear the white panel may be absent or hidden; the reference does not establish panels on multiple faces. An edge view will show a narrow rectangular column and may not permit exact identification. Match the inset only when the relevant face is visible.

confusable_with.name: potelet_moka_corten
confusable_with.distinction: Has open see-through rectangular voids, not a solid white inset panel.

limitations: Do not claim the panel is illuminated, reflective or present on every face.
Material and product functionality are not verified beyond the label and visible shape.

images.name: potelet_chatelet
images.visual_description: A very simple slender bollard with a smooth cylindrical shaft and a gently rounded or shallow-domed closed top. The body appears to continue directly into the top without an obvious separate cap, recessed neck, bright band or projecting ring. The reference is dark green, with minor surface wear. It is planted directly into the paving and has no conspicuous broad base plate, side loop or ornament. Recognition depends on the uninterrupted plain cylinder and subtly rounded crown, but those features are common and provide weaker model specificity than more ornate catalogue entries.
diagnostic_features: Plain uninterrupted round shaft
Gently rounded closed crown
No visible neck, bead, finial or side loop
Simple ground insertion
images.viewpoint_guidance: The cylinder is rotationally symmetric; the top profile is the main useful cue from any side. A high angle can make a flat top look rounded, so compare shading cautiously. If the crown is cropped or blurred, retain uncertainty among plain-post models.

confusable_with.name: potelet_inox_phenix
confusable_with.distinction: Reference has a bright brushed-metal surface and sharper flat-looking cap profile.

confusable_with.name: potelet_serie_2000_les_contemporains
confusable_with.distinction: Shows a distinct short top cap separated by a fine circular seam.

limitations: The reference is soft; lack of a visible seam is not definitive evidence that no seam exists.
Do not identify this model solely because a post is green.

images.name: potelet_city
images.visual_description: A slender grey cylindrical bollard with a short cylindrical cap whose upper edges are rounded. Immediately beneath the cap is a recessed dark neck followed by a conspicuous rounded bead or torus ring that projects around the shaft. Below this small head assembly, the shaft is smooth, narrow and uniform down to the ground. The cap, narrow neck and raised rounded bead create a stacked profile near the top. There is no wide hat brim, ball finial, side bicycle loop, or flared foot in the reference.
diagnostic_features: Short rounded cylindrical cap
Recessed neck directly below cap
Raised rounded bead below the neck
Straight slender shaft
images.viewpoint_guidance: Look for the three-level cap/neck/bead silhouette from either side. A high angle or blur can hide the bead and make it resemble an à-gorge post. The lower shaft provides little discrimination if the head is missing.

confusable_with.name: potelet_a_gorge
confusable_with.distinction: Very similar head-and-groove family; City shows a more distinct rounded projecting bead in this reference.

confusable_with.name: potelet_serie_2000_les_classiques
confusable_with.distinction: Traditional 2000 has a small bright mushroom-shaped cap instead of this tall cylindrical cap.

limitations: At low resolution, City versus the grooved entries may be ambiguous; do not overstate the subtle profile difference.

images.name: potelet_inox_phenix
images.visual_description: A plain upright cylindrical bollard with a bright silver, brushed-metal-looking finish. Long vertical highlights run down the smooth shaft. The top appears closed and flat or very slightly bevelled, with a relatively crisp rim and no separate neck, decorative cap, ring or finial. The body reaches directly into the paving without a conspicuous flared foot or large mounting plate. The shape is simple; the finish is helpful in the supplied catalogue but should not outweigh visible head geometry when lighting, dirt or paint changes the appearance.
diagnostic_features: Smooth round shaft with bright brushed-metal appearance
Closed flat-looking top with crisp rim
No groove, collar, ring or finial
No side attachment or broad base
images.viewpoint_guidance: Rotational symmetry makes the overall shape stable across azimuths, but specular reflections can change radically with view and lighting. From above, examine the plain closed top; from a distance, a bright highlight alone does not prove stainless steel.

confusable_with.name: potelet_chatelet
confusable_with.distinction: Reference has a softer rounded crown and painted dark surface, but geometry is close.

confusable_with.name: potelet_serie_2000_les_contemporains
confusable_with.distinction: Has a visible shallow circumferential cap seam near the top.

limitations: The label specifies inox, but alloy composition cannot be established from pixels.
Plain cylinders of unknown make can look similar.

images.name: potelet_moka_corten
images.visual_description: A narrow rust-brown rectangular open-frame bollard on a square or rectangular fixing plate. Two tall straight side strips are joined by a closed top, a transverse shelf-like divider near the upper portion, and a short solid lower section. The openings between the strips create a small upper rectangular window and a much taller lower rectangular window through which the background is visible. Its front therefore resembles a very narrow empty frame with two stacked apertures, rather than a solid post with a white insert. The dark depth of the flat metal members is visible along the sides.
diagnostic_features: Tall narrow rectangular open frame
Small upper and long lower see-through windows
Cross-divider near top and short solid foot
Rectangular base plate with corner bolts
images.viewpoint_guidance: The broad-face view reveals the two openings most clearly; from edge-on, they may disappear into a narrow strip. A bright background through an opening should not be mistaken for a white opaque panel. Check whether background features continue through the aperture.

confusable_with.name: potelet_borne_vision_corten
confusable_with.distinction: Solid column with an opaque white rectangular inset, not two open windows.

confusable_with.name: potelet_borne_velo_corten_cafe
confusable_with.distinction: Adds large circular side arcs to its split central frame.

limitations: Do not infer hidden light fixtures or other functionality from the shelf-like divider.
Rust-like finish is shared by several entries.

images.name: potelet_potelet
images.visual_description: An ornate dark rust-brown bollard topped by a large spherical ball on a short neck. Beneath the ball is a broad projecting disc-like shoulder or flange, below which the main shaft is thick and slightly tapering. Near the bottom a rounded ring separates the shaft from a stepped, flared base with angular or polygonal moulding. The lower plinth is wider than the shaft and appears faceted in the supplied view. Its heavy traditional silhouette contrasts with the thin plain modern posts. The large ball is the strongest single cue, supported by the broad shoulder and decorated base.
diagnostic_features: Large spherical top finial
Wide disc-like shoulder beneath ball
Thick slightly tapered shaft
Stepped flared/faceted lower base
images.viewpoint_guidance: The spherical finial is robust to view angle; the angular lower plinth may look different as faces rotate. If the top is cropped, the decorated base is supporting evidence but may not be sufficient. Patina, moss and rust spots are not permanent design features.

confusable_with.name: potelet_a_chapeau
confusable_with.distinction: Tiered hat-shaped head rather than a large sphere.

confusable_with.name: potelet_borne
confusable_with.distinction: Squat flat-topped cylinder with two thick raised rings, no ball.

limitations: The generic source name refers to this specific ornate reference; use potelet_a classifier for other models.

images.name: potelet_serie_2000_les_classiques
images.visual_description: A straight slender cylindrical bollard with a dark grey shaft and a small contrasting bright cap at the top. The cap has a low rounded mushroom or button-like profile, slightly wider than its narrow supporting neck. A short bright collar or stacked ring detail sits below it at the transition into the shaft. Most of the bollard is an undecorated uniform cylinder. The traditional cap assembly is restrained compared with a large ball or a wide tiered hat. The reference is narrow and somewhat blurred, so exact cap curvature should not be treated as a measured shape.
diagnostic_features: Small raised rounded mushroom/button cap
Narrow neck and short collar below cap
Plain cylindrical shaft
Contrasting bright head in reference
images.viewpoint_guidance: The rotational head profile should be similar from different sides. The bright finish can disappear in shade or after repainting; prioritize the raised cap and neck. From an overhead view the neck may be hidden, reducing separation from the contemporary version.

confusable_with.name: potelet_serie_2000_les_contemporains
confusable_with.distinction: Low nearly flush cylindrical cap with a fine seam, no pronounced mushroom neck.

confusable_with.name: potelet_a_chapeau
confusable_with.distinction: Much broader projecting tiered hat.

confusable_with.name: potelet_city
confusable_with.distinction: Taller cylindrical head and rounded bead rather than small mushroom button.

limitations: Small cap details may be unreliable in low-resolution query images.

images.name: potelet_serie_2000_les_contemporains
images.visual_description: A smooth grey cylindrical bollard with a shallow short cylindrical cap at the top. The cap has approximately the same diameter as the main shaft and a flat or gently rounded upper face. A fine horizontal circumferential seam or pair of very close lines separates it from the shaft just below the top. The silhouette is restrained, almost a plain cylinder: there is no pronounced narrowed neck, projecting mushroom, bead, ball or broad brim. The remainder of the post is straight and undecorated down to the ground.
diagnostic_features: Low cylindrical cap nearly flush with shaft
Fine circumferential seam immediately below cap
Plain straight round body
No pronounced projecting finial or recessed neck
images.viewpoint_guidance: The subtle seam is the useful cue around the post, but lighting or distance can erase it. From above, the cap can look identical to an ordinary closed cylinder. If the seam is unresolved, keep plain-post alternatives rather than declaring this model.

confusable_with.name: potelet_serie_2000_les_classiques
confusable_with.distinction: Raised mushroom/button cap on a narrow neck.

confusable_with.name: potelet_chatelet
confusable_with.distinction: No distinct separate cap seam is visible in its soft reference.

confusable_with.name: potelet_inox_phenix
confusable_with.distinction: Plain bright cylinder without a resolved cap seam in reference.

limitations: Apparent absence of a seam in a small query image is not a contradiction.
Paint and metallic highlights are secondary cues.
